ws3_mala_dispute.r90_report: Muse-to-Sarvam/ROUND-90-RELEASE-NUMBER.md: 'storing a dasham into a mala element does not convert and does not refuse — it stores the raw bits.' Program saved at ~/workspace/r90/probes/conv_mala.sm.
ws3_mala_dispute.r90_zero_explained: the '0' was the TREE COUNT ('Tree count for that trap: 0'), repeated by R95 ('Dasham → mala element stores: 0 in examples (R90's count still holds)'). Neither report says 'stores zero'.

results_on_v283.roundtrip_dasham_read: dasham back = a[0] then likha(back) prints 4615514078110652416.000000 — the dasham read converts the bits-as-integer to a double; it does NOT reinterpret the bits back to 3.7. The value 3.7 cannot be read back through any language read path.

ws3_mala_dispute.ruled_out: R38's 'a 3-cell mala silently returned 0' is a different, pre-fix alias finding (out-of-bounds load through an unmarked alias, fixed in R38), not the dasham-store referent.
ws3_mala_dispute.tree_count_note: every dasham-valued indexed store in examples/ and lib/ is into a kosh (135 kosh dasham ank_suchi; 140 kosh dasham ank_mala — name contains 'mala' but variable is a kosh; 148 kosh dasham ank_suchi; 110/118/123 t18 kosh tests; 252 w a kosh alias; lib kalana ok and samanvaya out, both kosh dasham). Stores into genuine malas are integers (248 a[i]=i+1; 251 a[0]=10; 246 x[0..7]; 20 nums[i]=i*i). 112 a[0]=d is into kosh a[1] (integer kosh, refuses E_DASHAM_VITTI for 4.8). 265 bahar[i]=buf stores a nirmmita pointer, refused E_SCRATCH_ESCAPE.
ws3_mala_dispute.verdict: neither side is wrong about the mechanism: raw qword store, no conversion, no refusal, unchanged v281→v283, literal and variable forms agree. The disagreement was a misreading of which '0' was which. The fix (if owners want one) is a mala-store check, not a zero-store fix.
